content.title: Management of ventricular arrhythmias and bradyarrhythmias (excerpt)

recommendations.text: Intravenous beta-blocker and/or amiodarone treatment is recommended for patients with polymorphic VT and/or VF unless contraindicated.
recommendations.notes: Acute management of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation.

recommendations.text: Prompt and complete revascularization is recommended to treat myocardial ischaemia that may be present in patients with recurrent VT and/or VF.
recommendations.notes: Target ischemia as a reversible cause of recurrent ventricular arrhythmia.

recommendations.text: Transvenous catheter pacing termination and/or overdrive pacing should be considered if VT cannot be controlled by repeated electrical cardioversion.
recommendations.notes: Consider pacing strategies when cardioversion fails to control VT.

recommendations.text: Radiofrequency catheter ablation at a specialized ablation centre followed by ICD implantation should be considered in patients with recurrent VT, VF, or electrical storm despite complete revascularization and optimal medical therapy.
recommendations.notes: Invasive ablation ± ICD for recurrent or refractory ventricular arrhythmias.

recommendations.text: Treatment of recurrent VT with haemodynamic relevance (despite repeated electrical cardioversion) with lidocaine may be considered if beta-blockers, amiodarone, and overdrive stimulation are not effective/applicable.
recommendations.notes: Lidocaine as an alternative antiarrhythmic in specific refractory cases.

recommendations.text: In patients with recurrent life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias, sedation or general anaesthesia to reduce sympathetic drive may be considered.
recommendations.notes: Use of sedation/anesthesia to blunt sympathetic triggers in recurrent life‑threatening arrhythmias.

recommendations.text: ICD implantation or the temporary use of a wearable cardioverter defibrillator may be considered <40 days after MI in selected patients (incomplete revascularization, pre-existing LVEF dysfunction, occurrence of arrhythmias >48 h after STEMI onset, polymorphic VT or VF).
recommendations.notes: Selected early post-MI use of ICD or wearable defibrillator for high-risk patients.

recommendations.text: Treatment of asymptomatic and haemodynamically irrelevant ventricular arrhythmias with anti-arrhythmic drugs is not recommended.
recommendations.notes: Avoid antiarrhythmic drug therapy for asymptomatic, hemodynamically insignificant ventricular ectopy.

recommendations.text: In cases of sinus bradycardia with haemodynamic intolerance or high-degree AV block without stable escape rhythm: i.v. positive chronotropic medication (adrenaline, vasopressin, and/or atropine) is recommended.
recommendations.notes: Acute pharmacologic increase of heart rate for haemodynamically significant bradycardia or high-degree AV block.
